thesis: Hold. Since the prior tick the pack adds one macro-relevant headline—U.S. junk bonds on track for their worst month since 2022 amid a global selloff—which reinforces credit-stress and volatility caution but does not name a conservative, diversified ETF sleeve I should add without a clearer catalyst. Remaining items are lifestyle columns, IPO commentary, and routine SEC 8-Ks (including Carnival Item 2.02 earnings disclosure); none provide a dated, actionable broad-market fact that overrides capital preservation. Context unchanged in spirit: VIX ~15.9 (modest), 10Y yield ~5.26% still elevated, oil/USO softer—consistent with a wait-and-see regime, not a prompt to deploy cash. Book: sizing equity ~$999.76, cash ~$750 (75%), one VTI line ~$249.74 (~25% of equity), already at this tier's 25% max single-name cap, so incremental VTI would breach roster limits and a new satellite would be headline-chasing. I propose no orders; consensus may act separately.
